COURTNEY EVANS

The Ex-Girlfriend
July 23, 1981 5'3" Northwood High (1999) EXILED

The "School Matt" Illusion

Courtney was Matt Miller's first genuine romantic connection. It is critical to note that before the bubble popped, she was not abusive; she was genuinely sweet and good for Matt. Inside their curated high school bubble, Courtney provided real, grounding physical affection, like gentle cheek kisses and hugs, which felt incredibly normalizing to Matt.

However, her attraction was heavily anchored to a highly curated, artificial version of his life. At Northwood High School, Matt’s complex medical needs were quietly managed by a retired male paraprofessional. While Courtney enjoyed Matt's personality and intelligence, she compartmentalized his severe dyspraxia and non-verbal status as background noise. She loved the idea of having Matt as a boyfriend but was completely unequipped to handle the heavy, clinical reality of his 24/7 care requirements outside of school.

The Omni-Q Betrayal

The superficial acceptance shattered when the relationship attempted to transition into the real world for a highly anticipated movie date in May 1999 to see The Paradigm. When Matt utilized his Vanguard LogicPad to inform her via Omni-Q that his 21-year-old sister, Sarah, would be accompanying them in her necessary role as his Private Duty Nurse, the teenage panic set in.

Lacking the maturity and vocabulary to process the clinical necessity of a care proxy, Courtney’s sheltered 18-year-old brain perceived the message as another, older woman crashing their romantic date. Blinded by a sudden wave of adolescent jealousy and insecurity, Courtney panicked and lashed out, sending a barrage of cruel, ableist messages directly to Matt's hard drive. It was a desperate, ugly defense mechanism that destroyed the trust instantly.

Realizing she had sabotaged a major relationship milestone (their shared 18th/21st birthday weekend), Courtney attempted to win Matt back at school by desperately offering a sexual encounter, proving she still didn't understand the depth of the boundary she had broken.

The Exile

Courtney drastically underestimated Matt's boundaries and the terrifying physical and legal power of his family. Matt fiercely rejected her inappropriate apology, prompting his retired male aide to physically step in and block her access to his wheelchair.

When Courtney later attempted to corner Matt at a local mall, she was intercepted by Sarah Miller. Standing a full 13 inches shorter than Sarah's 6'4" bodybuilder frame, Courtney was completely dwarfed. Utilizing her newly activated joint-and-several legal guardianship, Sarah threatened Courtney with a restraining order and harassment charges. Courtney was forced into a humiliating retreat and is permanently locked out of the Miller and Brooks family ecosystem.

Lore Notes

The pop-culture landscape of Courtney's era heavily features The Paradigm (the highly anticipated late-90s cyber-dystopian action movie) and The Final Note (a massive 1997-era historical romance blockbuster, the poster for which hangs prominently above Courtney's beige computer monitor). The communication vector for the betrayal was Omni-Q, the primary desktop instant messaging client used by teenagers in 1999.
